To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effective device parameters of conventional and pseudomorphic HEMTs on wafer can be extracted from the gate C-V measurement by comparison of the measured and simulated C-V characteristics.

the effective device parameters d A,N d,V b can be determined by fitting the C-V characteristic of the HEMT and that these parameters can be used for monitoring the wafer and for calibration of the design.

the gate C-V characteristic of HEMTs can be simulated accurately using self-consistently solved Schrodinger and poisson equations, and that the fit parameters d A,N and V b can be shown to describe the effective device parameters of the gate capacitance, and that this technique can be used to monitor the spatial variation of the fit parameters over the wafer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the C-V characteristics of conventional and pseudomorphic AlGaAs/GaAs HEMTs.
the study of the gate capacitance of conventional and pseudomorphic HEMTs and its dependence on the technological parameters.
the development of a new method for the evaluation of effective device parameters by comparison of measured and simulated C-V characteristics for conventional and pseudomorphic HEMTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a powerful and useful tool to monitor the technological parameters of the device and to optimize the process of fabrication.

the C-V method can be used as a powerful tool for the evaluation of the effective device parameters of pseudomorphic HEMTs, which is a very important step for the development of a pseudomorphic HEMT process.

the gate capacitance of pseudomorphic HEMTs is strongly influenced by the thickness of the doping layer d A, the doping density N D of the doped AlGaN layer and by the built-in voltage of the Schottky contact V b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can determine the effective device parameters of pseudomorphic HEMTs by comparison of measured and simulated C-V curves, and that we can use this technique for monitoring these parameters over the wafer and to calibrate the design of the devices.

the C-V measurements can be a powerful tool for the characterization of the device parameters and that this technique is very suitable for the development of a manufacturing process for pseudomorphic HEMTs and conventional HEMTs.

the effective device parameters can be obtained from the C-V characteristics and the effective device parameters obtained in this way can be used for the design and the calibration of the manufacturing process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-V technique is a powerful tool for the evaluation of the device parameters.
it can be applied to any device, and the effective parameters are those which are relevant to the device operation.
the effective device parameters can be determined by a simple and accurate procedure.
